title: Ops Check, Episode 2: The AGR Conversion, Part 2
desc: This one is long, but it's about your money. Congress is weighing a plan to phase out the Technician program and turn about nine out of ten full-time Guard jobs into AGR. Hiring stops in fiscal year 2028. The program is gone in 2038. So we ran the numbers on two Technicians, a mid-career mechanic and a new guy, and put them on the screen side by side. Same guy, two roads: stay a Technician, or go AGR. Yes, AGR pays more up front. In some places the best case even comes out ahead. But the best case takes twenty straight years, promotions on time, and a job waiting the day you get out. If your AGR tour gets cut short, and that is not your choice, you come up short by hundreds of thousands of dollars. The Technician's pension, supplement and match are set by law. The AGR deal is a stack of maybes. And that's before you count the rights you give up. Don't sign anything. Run your own numbers at calculator.local1776.org. Not a member, or dropped off? Join or rejoin at local1776.org/membership-portal. Then share this with everybody in your shop. #OpsCheck #LIUNA #Local1776 #NationalGuard #DualStatusTechnician #AGR #FederalEmployees #NDAA #KnowYourRights #UnionStrong #laborersrising #1u #AFLCIO

title: Ops Check: The AGR Conversion
desc: Congress is deciding whether to end the National Guard Technician program and convert our jobs to AGR. In this first episode of Ops Check, Ben Banchs, Business Manager-Secretary Treasurer of LIUNA Local 1776, breaks down why that's a bad deal for you, for the taxpayer, and for the Guard. What you need to know: • AGR comes with no guarantee. It takes 20 years of active duty to earn that retirement, and the Guard has no obligation to keep you that long. • A Technician job is a federal job. It can only be taken for cause, and you have the right to appeal. • Convert, and under this bill there's no coming back to your Technician job. • Run the numbers: even if the Guard keeps him all 20 years, an E-5 mechanic comes up hundreds of thousands to over a million dollars short over a lifetime. • It's not law yet. And even if it passes, it's voluntary. It takes your written consent, and the Guard can't pressure you or punish you for saying no. title: What Tuesday’s Election Means for Us | LIUNA Local 1776 Member Update
desc: Ben Banchs, Business Manager-Secretary Treasurer of LIUNA Local 1776, gives an update to our Technicians and Title 5 employees of the National Guard on what the November 2026 election means for federal sector collective bargaining and where we're headed. In this video: - Where we represent: nine National Guard states, Guam, the Professional Education Center in Little Rock, and National Guard Headquarters in Arlington - The two issues that have held us back: the March 2025 Executive Order on collective bargaining and the Technician to AGR Conversion - What a new Congress means for both - A word to management - What we're still doing for you every day: disciplinary cases, discrimination cases, and more Whether you've been with us this whole time, had to drop your dues when money got tight, or didn't know your deductions had stopped, this fight is about you. When the doors open back up, Local 1776 will be right back at the table, and we want you there with us. Something going on at work?
